Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

hey, could you put together a family dinner calendar for four weeks, from monday september 7 through sunday october 4, 2026? i need something we can actually use to decide dinner, not a general list of meal ideas. it’s Mara and Eli and our kids Nora, 12, and Sam, 8. Grandma Ruth joins us on Wednesdays, so plan five portions for those dinners and four for the others. The exception is the week of September 28: Ruth won’t be coming that Wednesday because we’ll all be at the school fundraiser instead.

please cover dinners only. Monday through Friday should have a dinner planned, except Wednesday, September 30, which should be labeled “No dinner planned — school fundraiser.” Saturdays are our catch-up nights, so just label them “leftovers or pantry night,” with no recipe or shopping-list ingredients for those days. Leave Sundays blank, rather than filling them with suggestions. We sometimes move meals around ourselves, so dates are useful, but don’t make the calendar depend on a particular order beyond the dates and the fixed events I’ve mentioned. I don’t need breakfasts, lunches, snacks, or a separate menu for Ruth.

A few food things matter. Nora can’t have cashews or pistachios because of a serious allergy; please avoid both and flag that packaged ingredients need their labels checked for them. That’s the specific allergy information we have, so don’t treat it as a general no-nuts rule. Eli dislikes mushrooms, so leave those out. Nora doesn’t like raw tomato, but cooked tomato is fine. Sam is happiest with rice, eggs, and mild curry, though he doesn’t need all three every week. Eli likes salmon and white fish. We are not asking for special diet meals for the children; the plan should work for all four of us, and Ruth can eat the same Wednesday dinner.

I’m trying to make the weeknights less chaotic, but not turn dinner into a project. As Eli put it, “please don't make every meal a project.” Keep the active weeknight work to about 35 minutes or less, not counting something that can be done ahead. A longer oven time is okay if the hands-on part stays short. Please give a short prep note so I can see what the work involves, but not full recipe cards. We have the usual oil, salt, pepper, dried oregano, cumin, rice, and pasta already; don’t count those as grocery purchases. Don’t assume we have other ingredients in the pantry.

We’d like two vegetarian dinners in each week of the calendar, with at least one on a Tuesday because Mara is vegetarian that night. Tuesday dinners should be vegetarian for everyone, not a separate plate. Don’t count Saturday leftovers or the fundraiser as a vegetarian meal. Please avoid using the same main protein on consecutive planned dinners. If the budget allows, include one fish dinner each week; it can be salmon or white fish. Our grocery target is about $165 per week for these dinners, not including the staples I mentioned. It’s a target, not a requirement to force a particular meal, and I know prices vary. Don’t add other dietary rules.

There are a couple of timing details. Ruth gets here around 6:15 on Wednesdays, so those meals should be ready then or able to stay warm without getting worse. She doesn’t like very spicy food. On Thursday, September 17, our oven is unavailable because it’s being repaired, so that date’s dinner needs to use another method. During the week of September 21, Mara gets home late Monday and Thursday. Those two dinners should either be make-ahead and reheatable or take no more than 20 minutes of active work when we get home. That shorter-time request is just for those two nights; the usual 35-minute guideline applies to the other weeknights.

Could you lay it out by week with each date, the meal title, and a brief prep note? Mark which planned dinners are vegetarian or fish, and identify anything that needs to be made ahead. Please include weekly grocery lists with approximate quantities, grouped under produce, refrigerated, pantry, and frozen where relevant. Avoid listing the same purchase twice within a week. We usually shop once a week, so organize each list for that week’s planned meals; omit Saturday ingredients and the fundraiser date. An approximate total against the $165 target would help, but I don’t need precise local pricing or a guarantee that it will stay under budget. If a cost can’t reasonably be estimated, just say it’s an estimate rather than making the list look exact.

One last thing: keep the calendar easy to print and scan. We’ll write changes on it by hand, so don’t add explanations after every meal or a long nutrition discussion. A compact note at the beginning can state the allergy reminder and the active-time guideline, but the dates and meal information should remain the focus. Please leave the Sunday spaces visibly blank and keep the final week’s fundraiser note in its dated Wednesday slot; don’t replace it with a meal or move it to a general note.", "output": "Create a practical, printable dinner calendar for Monday, September 7 through Sunday, October 4, 2026. Organize it by week and include each date, meal title, and a brief prep note. This is a four-week plan for Mara, Eli, Nora (12), and Sam (8). Plan four portions for ordinary dinners and five portions on Wednesdays, when Grandma Ruth joins them. Ruth will not visit on Wednesday, September 30, because the family will be at a school fundraiser.

## Calendar scope
- Plan dinners Monday through Friday, except Wednesday, September 30, which must read: “No dinner planned — school fundraiser.”
- Label every Saturday “leftovers or pantry night.” Do not provide a recipe or include Saturday ingredients in the grocery lists.
- Leave Sundays visibly blank.
- Do not include breakfasts, lunches, or snacks, or create a separate menu for Ruth. The family may move meals around, so use the dates without making the plan depend on a fixed sequence beyond the dates and events specified here.

## Food preferences and requirements
- Avoid cashews and pistachios because Nora has a serious allergy. Include a reminder to check packaged ingredient labels for both. Do not turn this into a general no-nuts rule.
- Leave mushrooms out because Eli dislikes them. Nora dislikes raw tomato; cooked tomato is fine.
- Sam enjoys rice, eggs, and mild curry. Eli likes salmon and white fish. These are preferences, not requirements to include all of them every week.
- Plan meals that work for the whole family. Ruth can eat the same Wednesday dinner, and she dislikes very spicy food.
- Include two vegetarian dinners in each calendar week, with at least one on Tuesday. Tuesday’s dinner should be vegetarian for everyone, not a separate meal for Mara, who is vegetarian on Tuesdays. Do not count Saturday leftovers or the fundraiser as a vegetarian dinner.
- Avoid using the same main protein on consecutive planned dinners. Include one salmon or white-fish dinner per week if it can fit the budget.

## Timing and preparation
Keep active weeknight work to about 35 minutes or less, excluding anything that can be prepared ahead. Longer oven cooking is acceptable if the hands-on work stays short. For Wednesday dinners, have the meal ready around Ruth’s 6:15 arrival or able to stay warm without getting worse.

The oven will be unavailable on Thursday, September 17, so use another cooking method for that dinner. During the week of September 21, Mara gets home late on Monday and Thursday. For those two dates, choose dinners that can be made ahead and reheated, or require no more than 20 minutes of active work after the family gets home. The 20-minute limit applies only to those two dinners; use the usual 35-minute guideline on the other weeknights. Include brief prep notes, but do not provide full recipe cards.

## Budget and shopping lists
The grocery target is about $165 per week for the planned dinners, excluding these staples already on hand: oil, salt, pepper, dried oregano, cumin, rice, and pasta. Do not assume other pantry ingredients are available. Treat the budget as a target, not a reason to force a particular meal; prices vary. For each week, provide a grocery list with approximate quantities, grouped under Produce, Refrigerated, Pantry, and Frozen where relevant. Avoid duplicating a purchase within a week, and omit ingredients for Saturdays and the fundraiser date. Include an approximate weekly total against the target. If a cost cannot reasonably be estimated, identify it as an estimate rather than implying precision.

Keep the calendar easy to scan and print, with dates and meal details as the focus. A compact opening note may state the allergy reminder and active-time guideline. Avoid explanations after every meal and a long nutrition discussion. Keep the fundraiser entry in its dated Wednesday slot, do not replace it with a meal or move it to a general note, and leave the Sunday spaces blank."}]
